description: §1.5, Example 1.12 (rec12 P2), part (a), the parenthetical immediately after the [SOLUTION GAP] fill (fragment g4_s1.html line 454): "the antiderivative is $1+\frac{e^{-\lambda z}}{2}e^{-2\lambda y}$ evaluated between $y=0$ and $y=\infty$, giving $(1+0)-(0+\frac{e^{-\lambda z}}{2})$". This evaluation is arithmetically incoherent: the stated expression at $y=0$ equals $1+e^{-\lambda z}/2$, not $0+e^{-\lambda z}/2$, so the printed bracket would give $-e^{-\lambda z}/2$, not $1-\tfrac12 e^{-\lambda z}$. The hedge "once the constant of the first piece is included" does not repair it. The genuine antiderivative of $\lambda e^{-\lambda y}-\lambda e^{-\lambda z}e^{-2\lambda y}$ is $-e^{-\lambda y}+\tfrac{e^{-\lambda z}}{2}e^{-2\lambda y}$, whose evaluation $[\,]_0^\infty$ is $0-(-1+\tfrac{e^{-\lambda z}}{2})=1-\tfrac12 e^{-\lambda z}$. Correct fix: say plainly that the source's printed "1" is not a constant of integration but the already-evaluated value of $\int_0^\infty\lambda e^{-\lambda y}dy=1$, and give the true antiderivative with its two limits.

§2.1 duplicates §1 wholesale with no cross-reference. Example 2.2 (rec13 P2) re-derives the two-break stick from scratch — $\mathbb{E}[X\mid Y]=Y/2$, $\mathbb{E}[X]=\ell/4$, $\operatorname{var}(\mathbb{E}[X\mid Y])=\ell^2/48$, $\mathbb{E}[\operatorname{var}(X\mid Y)]=\ell^2/36$, $\operatorname{var}(X)=7\ell^2/144$ — which §1 already does in full in Example 1.2, Example 1.4 and Example 1.9 (same numbers, same steps, same B&T Example 4.17 citation). Practice 2.1 is likewise a verbatim repeat of Practice 1.6 (third break, $\ell/8$ and $37\ell^2/1728$), even down to the same 'independent check' via $X=\ell U_1U_2U_3$. Neither §2 item acknowledges the §1 treatment, and the two are backed by different compute scripts producing different MC values (g4_s1.json stick_varX_mc=0.048538 / pr4_varX3_mc=0.021353 vs g4_s2.json stick2_mc_var=0.048662 / stick3_mc_var=0.021422), so a reader meeting them twice sees inconsistent-looking simulation figures. Example 2.2 should be reduced to the rec13-specific framing plus a pointer to §1.4/§1.9 (or §1 should defer to §2), and Practice 2.1 should be dropped or cross-referenced to Practice 1.6.

The §0 srcref line understates the sources actually used, in three of its four lecture entries. It declares 'L12 slides 1–5 · L13 slides 1–6 · L14 slides 1, 4, 7 · L15 slides 1–2', but the body cites L12 slide 6 (§0.1 closing sentence, 'the unfinished two-piece-density example of L12 slide 6') and L12 slides 7–8 (three times: the random-sum paragraph, the capital/lowercase Gotcha, the Fig. 0.1 caption and the §2 roadmap bullet); L14 slides 3–6 (Table 0.1's own figcap says so explicitly, and the Counts bullet cites 'L14 slide 5'); and L15 slide 3 (the Interarrival-times bullet, 'the L15 slide 3 fishing rate'). Per the style contract the srcref is the section-level source declaration; it must read at least L12 slides 1–8, L14 slides 1, 3–7, L15 slides 1–3.

Table 0.1's caption lists its completion sources as 'L13 slides 4–6, L14 slides 3–6 and L15 slide 2', but the table's last row (Merging / splitting) is drawn from L13 slides 7–8 (Bernoulli split/merge, 'collisions are counted as one arrival'), L14 slide 8 and L15 slides 4 and 6 (Poisson merging at rate $\lambda_1+\lambda_2$, splitting at $p\lambda$/$(1-p)\lambda$) — none of which appear in the caption's source list. The §0.3 sentence 'Each section also works its associated recitation problems in full inside collapsible solution boxes; the recitation material for this block covers iterated expectations and total variance, the Bernoulli process with random sums and coupon collecting, and exponentials, Erlangs and Poisson merging/splitting' misdescribes the block in two ways. (ii) 'Each section works its associated recitation problems' is not what happens: rec14 (mosquito/tick Bernoulli merging, Al's Pascal and random-sum problem, coupon collector) is pure Bernoulli-process/random-sum material owned by §2, yet it is worked in §3.5 (g4_s3.html Examples 3.7–3.9), and §2 never points the reader there.

Fig. 2.3's caption (g4_s2.html line 487) says 'The first three interarrival times $T_1,T_2,T_3$ of §2.4 are marked', but §2.4 defines only $T_1$ (the first-success time); $T_2,T_3$ and the general interarrival sequence are introduced in §2.5 ('Following L13 slide 6, let $T_1$ be… $T_2$ the number of additional trials…'). Example 1.11's title reads 'rec12 P1 — the correlation coefficient is unchanged by an affine change of units', which its own body then refutes: the derivation ends at $\rho(aX+b,Y)=\operatorname{sign}(a)\,\rho(X,Y)$, and the [SOURCE TYPO?] paragraph explicitly adjudicates that invariance holds only for $a>0$ while $a<0$ flips the sign (the cheatsheet states it correctly). The heading should be qualified, e.g. '…unchanged by an affine change of units with positive scale'.

§1.1, Property item 1 ('Pulling out what is known') closes with 'See B&T Problem 4.25.' That book problem number appears nowhere else in the note and is not among the B&T problems declared in the §1 srcref (which lists only Problem 4.16, p. 248 and Problem 4.20, p. 250, both anchored by rec12). §2.4, Example 2.9 ('fresh start at a random time'): $N$ is defined as the first $i$ with $X_{i-1}=X_i=1$, so $N\ge2$ with probability 1, yet the rigorous route writes the total-probability decomposition as $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mathbf{P}(N=n)\,\mathbf{P}(X_{n+1}=X_{n+2}=0\mid N=n)$ and then 'using $\sum_{n\ge1}\mathbf{P}(N=n)=1$'. The $n=1$ term has $\mathbf{P}(N=1)=0$ and the conditioning event is empty, so the sum should start at $n=2$; as written it conditions on a null event.

Twelve broken internal cross-references, concentrated in exactly the section advertised as 'the one page to revise from'. In the §5.1 identity table the §1 pointers are all shifted one subsection late: 'Law of iterated expectations … §1.3' and 'Total expectation theorem … §1.3' (line 36–37) should be §1.2; 'var(X|Y=y) … §1.4' and 'var(X|Y) … §1.4' (lines 38–39) should be §1.3; 'Law of total variance … §1.5' (line 40) should be §1.3 (§1.5 is the rec12 section); 'Random sum E[Y|N]=N E[X] … §2.1' (line 41) should be §2.2 (§2.1 is the rec13 P1–P2 warm-up). Gotcha 1 (line 175) likewise cites '(§1.3)' for the law of iterated expectations; should be §1.2. In the §5.2 correspondence table every Poisson-column pointer is wrong: 'Time to the first arrival … §4.2' and 'Memorylessness … §4.2' (lines 122, 124) should be §3.3 (§4.2 is Merging); 'Time to the kth arrival … §4.3' (line 123) should be §3.4 (§4.3 is Splitting); 'Merging two independent streams … §4.1' (line 125) should be §4.2 and 'Splitting … §4.1' (line 126) should be §4.3 (§4.1 is the Poisson-fishing warm-up); 'Random incidence … §4.5' (line 127) should be §4.4 for the Poisson/Erlang(2) result, with §4.5 only for the renewal generalization. The §2, §3.1 and §3.2 pointers in the same tables are correct, so a reader has no way to know which pointers to distrust. All §-references inside s1–s4 were checked and are correct; the defect is isolated to g4_s5.html.

§5.2 correspondence table, 'Random incidence' row, Bernoulli cell (line 127) asserts 'the slot you land in is unremarkable, but the gap you land in is length-biased in the same way', cited to 'L15 s7, s8; §4.5'. Both cited sources are purely continuous-time (Poisson/renewal); §2 never treats random incidence for the Bernoulli process at all, so this is the one claim in the synthesis table that is stated nowhere else in the note and never derived. It is also imprecise: for a Bernoulli(p) process the length-biased gap PMF is p_L(l) = l·p^2(1-p)^{l-1} (a Pascal-of-order-2 shape), not simply 'the same' as the Erlang(2) statement in the adjacent cell. Correct looks like either deriving the discrete length-bias in §2.6 (three lines, using p_L(l)=l·p_T(l)/E[T] with E[T]=1/p) and citing that, or replacing the cell with an explicit forward pointer that says the Bernoulli case is not covered.

§1.4 ('The lecture's worked and unworked examples') is the only non-recitation topic subsection in §1–§4 with neither a `note` (Interpretation/Intuition) box nor a `warn` (Gotcha) box — box inventory: note=0, warn=0, recipe=0.
